God has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection. What does this living hope mean to you?
Your faith is tested like gold in fire. How has testing strengthened your faith?
Peter says, "Be holy in all your conduct." What does holiness look like in your everyday life?
You were ransomed with the precious blood of Christ. What does that tell you about your worth to God?
Peter says to long for pure spiritual milk. How can you grow your hunger for God's word?
You are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, God's own possession. Which of these titles speaks to you?
Peter urges good conduct so others may see and glorify God. How can your life point others to God?
Christ suffered for you, leaving an example. How can you follow in his steps when treated unfairly?
Peter describes the beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit and honouring one another. How can you honour those closest to you?
Do not repay evil for evil, but bless. Who can you bless instead of resent?
Always be prepared to give a reason for your hope, with gentleness and respect. How would you explain your hope?
Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. What does this mean for you?
Peter says to live for the will of God, not human passions. What does that look like this week?
Love covers a multitude of sins; use your gifts to serve one another. What gift can you use to serve?
Peter says not to be surprised at fiery trials. How does sharing in Christ's sufferings bring joy?
Entrust your soul to a faithful Creator while doing good. What do you need to entrust to him?
Peter urges leaders to shepherd the flock willingly and eagerly. How can you care for others God has placed around you?
"Cast all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you." What anxiety can you cast on him today?
Your adversary prowls like a roaring lion; resist him, firm in faith. How can you stay alert?
After you have suffered a little while, God will restore and strengthen you. Where do you need his restoring?
